purpose: Where each AC-11 axis envelope comes from, so a CI lane can assemble the aggregator's manifest instead of a person assembling it by hand. tools/aggregate_ac11_evidence.py has never been run by CI (48-task rescore v1.8 §4-5-3), which is why its recomputed PASS count is 0/8 -- not because the axes fail, but because nothing calls it. This file is the input that makes calling it possible, and it is deliberately honest about the axes that have no measurement means yet: naming them here with the reason is what keeps the aggregator's INVALID_RUN legible instead of mysterious.
note: chain is the measured state of the producer -> workflow -> importer path, read from the tree rather than asserted -- and 'the importer exists' is not the same as 'the importer emits an axis envelope', which is the mistake r1 caught. envelopeShape records what the importer actually writes: 'axis-evidence' is one envelope, 'axes-bundle' is a wrapper whose axes array holds them, and 'not-an-axis-envelope' means the importer's output cannot go into the aggregator at all. 'complete' therefore requires producer, workflow, importer AND an admissible shape. The aggregator requires all eight envelopes and refuses otherwise, so an incomplete or absent axis makes the run INVALID_RUN by design -- that is the fail-closed answer, and the reason text is what tells the reader what is in the way. importerEmitsAxes is read from the importer file as an EXACT set, not as a subset: r1 only checked that each claimed name appears somewhere, so a migration row naming one of its two axes stayed true while describing half the chain (#299 r2). A row with no importer emits nothing, so its set is empty however much its producer names. Card 216 closed the security chain: the importer now adapts the producer's report into an axis envelope (runPurpose ac11-axis-evidence, the reviewed target registry, the artifact digests it already measured), so the chain is complete in the sense this file means -- an admissible envelope exists. The axis still does not pass, for a different and narrower reason: the aggregator requires four threat reports and only SEC-SCAN-001 has a producer anywhere in this repository, so the envelope's verdict is NOT_OBSERVED and names the three that are missing. 'complete' is about the chain, not about the verdict. Measured at 097da87d with the real run 36943527856: the assembler now puts this axis into the manifest (assembledAxes names it for the first time) and the aggregator evaluates it instead of reporting it missing. r1 of that review measured what the card had left open: the aggregator refused the envelope at the common-envelope stage with 'environment.comparableGroup is required' -- INVALID_RUN, which is not an admissible envelope however complete the chain looked in this file. The aggregator requires that group on every axis envelope and the security producer does not write one, so the importer now declares this lane's group the way the accessibility and migration importers declare theirs (tools/import_ac11_accessibility_evidence.py, tools/import_ac11_migration_rehearsal.py), and only after checking that the report's environment satisfies the environment the reviewed registry requires for this target -- the name describes a set whose membership was checked rather than assumed. Re-measured at 626cbc5c with run 36949022989: the importer writes NOT_OBSERVED, the assembler names this axis in assembledAxes, and the aggregator recomputes NOT_OBSERVED for it, so the only run-level complaint left is the seven axes that are absent. The envelope also names the importer blob that wrote it and the aggregator refuses one the source tree does not contain, which is what the reviewed scan allowlist's stale pins hid: 0f614152 moved the workflow and 8933b6bd moved the importer while the pins stayed where they were, and every report copies those three pins into toolFiles, so the drift was an INVALID_RUN waiting for the three missing producers to arrive. The pins are rotated to the measured blobs and a ratchet test holds them there. The importer also stops passing a verdict through: it recomputes SEC-SCAN-001 from the payload the artifact carries and refuses to answer for the three threat reports it cannot recompute, so four rows carrying nothing but a threat ID can no longer become MEASURED_PASS. r2 measured one more thing the importer was not reading: its recomputation looked at the two counts and the four inventory lengths only, so a payload carrying a finding row nobody counted, and one whose scanners read no files and no dependencies, both recomputed MEASURED_PASS. The payload arithmetic now lives in one function in the aggregator, scan_payload_invariants, which the importer calls as well, so the two validators of 'critical and high are zero' cannot drift: the finding rows bind to the two counts, the counts to the per-scanner summaries, the summaries to the two scanner exit codes, and the coverage inventories to the files and dependencies the scanners actually read, with an empty inventory refused rather than passed. Re-measured at 3ae6b316 with run 36951113824: the axis is still NOT_OBSERVED to the aggregator, and both of the review's probes, applied to the real artifact bytes and re-signed, are refused by the invariant they break.

axes.reason: Producer and importer both exist, but the importer accepts only the dry-run report (import_ac11_composite_long_soak.py refuses any other runPurpose) and the envelope it writes is reference-only NOT_OBSERVED, so what is missing is the run AND the import branch that would read it -- and no hosted runner can produce that run (card 217, measured against the registered target s11-ac11-composite-long-soak-v0). The target requires windowSeconds >= 86400 -- 24 hours against GitHub's 6-hour job limit -- and requiredEnvironment.topology 'physical-five-node' with windowClass 'physical-24h', 5 registered / 4 eligible / 1 excluded nodes and one CP-colocated node. Several criteria cannot exist on a hosted VM at all: thermal headroom and throttle seconds, planned power-fault cases with a recovery bound, switch and WAN fault cases, and externalObserverCoveragePpm with observer 'external-monotonic-v1', which has to sit outside the measured population. faultInjection 'controlled-v1' is the G-24 adapter this repository does not own, and the producer already says so: `--mode physical` exits 2 with verdict BLOCKED_EXTERNAL, blocker G-19, 'five-node inventory is missing; no physical action was started' (measured on this PC). So a hosted workflow would be a workflow that cannot produce the evidence, and the axis definition is not lowered to fit one. The intranet execution procedure is docs/vault/40_Operations/AC-11_long-soak_사내망_실행_절차.md.
